To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lightweight feature vectors based on the length of the packet, instead of the classic flow profiles, are more effective for the detection of malicious traffic in networks, and that the accuracy and speed of the current vectors can be improved.
lightweight feature sets based on source behavior, packet length, and packet inter-arrival time can be used for accurate detection of attacks in network traffic.

(i) the UNSW-Network-Behaviour-15 dataset is a good benchmark for attack detection, (ii) features based on flow duration and packet length are determinant for attack detection, and (iii) analysis based on source behaviour instead of flow profiles is a better approach for attack detection in encrypted traffic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of lightweight feature sets for attack detection.
the development of lightweight feature vectors for attack detection in network traffic, which are easy to process and analyze, allowing to generate them even from encrypted traffic.
the development of lightweight feature sets for early detection of malicious activity in network traffic, with the purpose of improving the performance of intrusion detection systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best features for attack detection in network traffic are those related to the length of packets.
the most important features are those that are related to packet size, and those that are based on source behavior.
, for attack detection, it is better to use features based on source behavior, rather than classic features based on flow profiles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for network attack detection, it is not necessary to use all the features proposed in the literature, as some of them are redundant or not relevant.
the most important feature for attack detection is not the destination port, but the packet length.
the use of source behavior features, and the analysis of packet length are the most effective and lightweight approaches for early attack detection in network traffic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selection of the feature vector is a critical task for machine learning-based network security.
the features to be used for attack detection can be selected based on a meta-analysis of the existing literature, and that the use of packet length features is determinant for attack detection.
, in the future, lightweight feature vectors should be designed to capture source behavior instead of flow profiles.
